510_year_evolution.promulgator: Duke Wilhelm IV & Duke Ludwig X of Bavaria
510_year_evolution.key_doctrine: Only Water, Malted Barley, and Hops permitted. Prohibits toxic herbs (henbane, belladonna) and reserves wheat/rye strictly for bakers.
Discovered that yeast is a living micro-organism causing alcoholic fermentation. Yeast officially codified as the 4th indispensable ingredient.
Unified Bavarian Reinheitsgebot across all German states. Established bottom-fermenting vs top-fermenting malt allowances.
Commission v. Germany: Ruled that non-German beers containing adjuncts could not be banned from sale under EU free movement of goods, but German brewers voluntarily maintained the 1516 purity seal.
Modern statutory codification: Bottom-fermented beers restricted to barley malt, hops, yeast, and water. Traditional top-fermented beers permitted other malted grains.

510_year_evolution.key_doctrine: Statutory law as executable code. Automated GitHub Actions linters audit craft recipes against 510-year purity standards and issue SHA-256 seals.

scotus_jurisprudence.holding: States cannot discriminate against out-of-state producers by banning out-of-state direct beverage shipment while allowing in-state shipment.
scotus_jurisprudence.impact: Unlocks interstate direct-to-consumer craft distribution networks.

scotus_jurisprudence.case: Tennessee Wine and Spirits Retailers Assn. v. Thomas, 139 S. Ct. 2449 (2019)
scotus_jurisprudence.topic: Durational Residency Requirements for Beverage Licenses
scotus_jurisprudence.holding: The 21st Amendment does not shield state protectionist licensing requirements that burden interstate commerce.
scotus_jurisprudence.impact: Expands interstate craft brewhouse capital investment and national taproom ownership.

scotus_jurisprudence.case: Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo, 144 S. Ct. 2244 (2024)
scotus_jurisprudence.holding: Courts must exercise independent judgment rather than deferring to agency interpretations of ambiguous statutes.
scotus_jurisprudence.impact: Reshapes TTB (Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau) and FDA rule enforcement on labeling, food additives, and craft brewing trade practices.
